Le truffe usano sempre la fretta. Tre do: Scams always use a rush. Three questions and one rule about codes are enough to spot them.

<strong>SMS da SpediLù: «Il tuo pacco è: Text from LuParcel: “Your parcel is held. Pay €1.99 today: luparcel.parcel-delivery.top/pay” Scam. A rush, money and an address that isn’t the courier’s.
<strong>WhatsApp da «Marco»: «Scusa, ti: WhatsApp from “Marco”: “Sorry, a code reached you by mistake, can you send it over?” Scam. It’s the code scam: Marco’s account has already been stolen. Call Marco on the number you know.
<strong>Email da PixelArena: «Il tuo acc: Email from PixelArena: “Your account will be closed in 24 hours. Enter your password here to confirm.” Scam. A threat, a rush and a password request: no game asks for your password by email.
<strong>SMS: «Hai vinto uno smartphone!: Text: “You’ve won a smartphone! Reply with your name and address for delivery.” Scam. A prize you never entered and a request for details: too good to be true.
<strong>Nell’app ufficiale del gioco, ap: In the game’s official app, opened by you: “New login from another device. Is that you?” Genuine, if I check it in the official channel. It comes from the app you opened yourself. If it isn’t you, say no, change your password and tell an adult.
<strong>Sul registro elettronico, aperto: In the school’s online register, opened by you: “School trip tomorrow, permission slip to sign.” Genuine, if I check it in the official channel. An official channel you opened yourself, no strange rush, no link to tap.
Perché quasi tutte le truffe mettono fre: Why do almost all scams rush you?
<strong>Dove portare la classe:</strong>: Where to take the class: When you rush, you don’t stop to check. Honest people give you time to check.
Se hai già cliccato o dato un codice, è: If you’ve already tapped or given a code, is it too late?
<strong>Dove portare la classe:</strong>: Where to take the class: No. Tell an adult straight away, change the password from the official app and warn your friends. It happens to adults too: it isn’t your fault, it’s a well-made trick (stage 10, “If it happens”).
Where to take the class: Opening the official app or site yourself, calling your friend on the number you know, asking an adult. Never using the link or number in the suspicious message.
Se uno studente racconta qualcosa: If a student tells you something
Ascolta con calma e ringrazia per la fid: Listen calmly and thank them for trusting you. Don’t press with questions and don’t promise to keep it secret: explain that you’ll talk to someone who can help. Follow your school’s procedure and tell the bullying and cyberbullying contact person.
Usa quattro carte e lascia le tre domand: Use four cards and keep the three questions on the board for the whole lesson.
In terza leggete gli indirizzi dei link: With older students read link addresses from the right (the part before the first slash) and discover that a caller’s number on screen can be faked.
Carte lette ad alta voce in coppia; chi: Cards read aloud in pairs; anyone who struggles to write can answer aloud or with a drawing.
